findings.summary: COT prompt (chain-of-thought instructions) is silently dropped when building chat formatter for reasoning-capable (R1-style) models
findings.failure_scenario: User selects a chain-of-thought prompt for a reasoning-capable model (e.g. DeepSeek R1, QwQ, Qwen3). `build_chat_formatter` line 236 passes `thinking_instructions=cot_prompt` to `get_chat_formatter`, but `get_chat_formatter` at line 217 does NOT forward `thinking_instructions` to `SingleTurnR1ThinkingFormatter(system_message, user_input)`. The old `run_strategy()` returned 'cot_as_message' and the COT prompt was appended as a system message; the new code drops it entirely. The formatter's `next_turn()` never includes thinking instructions in the message list, so the model receives no COT guidance despite the user selecting a chain-of-thought prompt.

findings.summary: generate_json_schema_message mutates its input parameter in-place by overwriting training_chat[-1].content
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a `training_chat` list to `generate_json_schema_message`, which sets `training_chat[-1].content = json_string` (re-formatting the JSON). If the caller subsequently processes the same chat list — for example by passing it to another format generator — the last message's content has been silently altered from the original model output to a re-serialized compact JSON string. This could corrupt multi-format dataset generation or confuse debugging.

findings.summary: TwoMessageCotFormatter and TwoMessageCotLegacyFormatter raise ValueError referencing the old enum name 'final_and_intermediate' instead of the current strategy names
findings.failure_scenario: A user or developer passes `thinking_instructions=None` with strategy `two_message_cot` (the new enum value). Both formatters at lines 92-94 and 138-140 raise `ValueError("thinking_instructions are required when strategy is final_and_intermediate")`. The message references 'final_and_intermediate' which is no longer a user-facing strategy name (`ChatStrategy.two_message_cot_legacy` has that value, but `ChatStrategy.two_message_cot` has value 'two_message_cot'). This misleads debugging — the error name does not match the strategy the caller actually used.

findings.summary: R1-style thinking guard removed from generate_vertex_gemini; Vertex training data may be generated for R1 models without backend validation
findings.failure_scenario: Old code raised `ValueError("R1 style thinking is not supported for Vertex Gemini.")` when `thinking_r1_style` was True. The new code has no such guard — `generate_vertex_gemini` will produce Vertex-format training data with R1 content (e.g. `<think>...</think>` tags embedded in the assistant message). While the Svelte UI filters R1 out of Vertex download options, the backend API endpoint accepts the combination without validation. A direct API call or future UI change could produce training data that Vertex Gemini cannot parse correctly.
